## 6. Delete Pattern

```python
"""
DELETE PATTERN
Purpose: Remove rows from Delta tables with ACID guarantees.
Use Cases:
- GDPR compliance (right to be forgotten)
- Data retention policies
- Data cleanup
- Soft deletes
"""

class DeltaDeletePattern:
    def __init__(self, spark, base_path):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_path = base_path
        self.table_path = f"{base_path}/delete_demo"
    
    def create_sample_table(self):
        """Create a sample table for delete operations."""
        print("Creating sample table...")
        
        data = [
            (1, "Alice", "alice@email.com", "2024-01-01", "active"),
            (2, "Bob", "bob@email.com", "2024-01-15", "active"),
            (3, "Charlie", "charlie@email.com", "2023-06-01", "active"),
            (4, "David", "david@email.com", "2023-01-01", "inactive"),
            (5, "Eve", "eve@email.com", "2024-02-01", "active"),
            (6, "Frank", "frank@email.com", "2022-12-01", "inactive"),
            (7, "Grace", "grace@email.com", "2024-03-01", "active"),
            (8, "Henry", "henry@email.com", "2023-05-01", "pending_deletion"),
            (9, "Ivy", "ivy@email.com", "2023-08-01", "active"),
            (10, "Jack", "jack@email.com", "2022-06-01", "inactive")
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, [
            "user_id", "name", "email", "created_date", "status"
        ])
        
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(self.table_path)
        
        print("Sample table created")
        print("\nInitial Table:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path).show()
    
    def perform_simple_delete(self):
        """Perform simple delete operation."""
        print("\n=== PERFORMING SIMPLE DELETE ===")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, self.table_path)
        
        # Delete users with 'pending_deletion' status
        print("Deleting users with status 'pending_deletion'...")
        delta_table.delete("status = 'pending_deletion'")
        
        print("\nTable After Simple Delete:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path).orderBy("user_id").show()
    
    def perform_conditional_delete(self):
        """Perform delete with complex conditions."""
        print("\n=== PERFORMING CONDITIONAL DELETE ===")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, self.table_path)
        
        # Delete inactive users created before 2023
        print("Deleting inactive users created before 2023...")
        delta_table.delete(
            "status = 'inactive' AND created_date < '2023-01-01'"
        )
        
        print("\nTable After Conditional Delete:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path).orderBy("user_id").show()
    
    def perform_delete_with_subquery(self):
        """Perform delete using subquery."""
        print("\n=== PERFORMING DELETE WITH SUBQUERY ===")
        
        # Create a separate table with user IDs to delete
        users_to_delete = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            (4,), (6,)
        ], ["user_id"])
        
        users_to_delete.createOrReplaceTempView("users_to_delete")
        
        # Register Delta table as temp view
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path).createOrReplaceTempView("users_table")
        
        # Delete using SQL with subquery
        print("Deleting users based on subquery...")
        self.spark.sql(f"""
            DELETE FROM delta.`{self.table_path}`
            WHERE user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM users_to_delete)
        """)
        
        print("\nTable After Subquery Delete:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path).orderBy("user_id").show()
    
    def implement_soft_delete(self):
        """Implement soft delete pattern."""
        print("\n=== IMPLEMENTING SOFT DELETE PATTERN ===")
        
        soft_delete_path = f"{self.base_path}/soft_delete_demo"
        
        # Create table with deleted flag
        data = [
            (1, "Alice", "alice@email.com", False, None),
            (2, "Bob", "bob@email.com", False, None),
            (3, "Charlie", "charlie@email.com", False, None),
            (4, "David", "david@email.com", False, None),
            (5, "Eve", "eve@email.com", False, None)
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, [
            "user_id", "name", "email", "is_deleted", "deleted_at"
        ])
        
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(soft_delete_path)
        
        print("Initial Table with Soft Delete Support:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(soft_delete_path).show()
        
        # Perform soft delete (update instead of delete)
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, soft_delete_path)
        
        print("\nPerforming soft delete on user_id = 2 and 4...")
        delta_table.update(
            condition="user_id IN (2, 4)",
            set={
```python
                "is_deleted": "true",
                "deleted_at": "current_timestamp()"
            }
        )
        
        print("\nTable After Soft Delete:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(soft_delete_path).show()
        
        print("\nActive Users Only (Filtered View):")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(soft_delete_path) \
            .filter("is_deleted = false") \
            .show()
        
        # Demonstrate recovery from soft delete
        print("\nRecovering user_id = 2 from soft delete...")
        delta_table.update(
            condition="user_id = 2",
            set={
                "is_deleted": "false",
                "deleted_at": "null"
            }
        )
        
        print("\nTable After Recovery:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(soft_delete_path).show()
    
    def perform_partition_delete(self):
        """Perform efficient partition-level delete."""
        print("\n=== PERFORMING PARTITION DELETE ===")
        
        partition_table_path = f"{self.base_path}/partition_delete_demo"
        
        # Create partitioned table
        data = []
        for year in [2022, 2023, 2024]:
            for month in range(1, 13):
                for i in range(10):
                    data.append((
                        year * 10000 + month * 100 + i,
                        f"User_{year}_{month}_{i}",
                        year,
                        month
                    ))
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "name", "year", "month"])
        
        df.write.format("delta") \
            .partitionBy("year", "month") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .save(partition_table_path)
        
        print(f"Created partitioned table with {df.count()} records")
        
        # Show partition summary
        print("\nPartition Summary Before Delete:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(partition_table_path) \
            .groupBy("year", "month").count() \
            .orderBy("year", "month") \
            .show(5)
        
        # Delete entire partition (very efficient)
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, partition_table_path)
        
        print("\nDeleting all data from year 2022...")
        delta_table.delete("year = 2022")
        
        print("\nPartition Summary After Delete:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(partition_table_path) \
            .groupBy("year", "month").count() \
            .orderBy("year", "month") \
            .show(5)
        
        total_after = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(partition_table_path).count()
        print(f"\nTotal records after partition delete: {total_after}")
    
    def demonstrate_delete_metrics(self):
        """Demonstrate delete operation metrics."""
        print("\n=== DELETE OPERATION METRICS ===")
        
        # Reset table
        self.create_sample_table()
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, self.table_path)
        
        # Perform delete
        print("Deleting inactive users...")
        delta_table.delete("status = 'inactive'")
        
        # Get metrics from history
        history = delta_table.history(1)
        metrics = history.select("operationMetrics").collect()[0][0]
        
        print("\nDelete Operation Metrics:")
        print(f"Number of deleted rows: {metrics.get('numDeletedRows', 0)}")
        print(f"Number of files removed: {metrics.get('numRemovedFiles', 0)}")
        print(f"Number of files added: {metrics.get('numAddedFiles', 0)}")
        
        # Show operation details
        print("\nOperation Details:")
        history.select("version", "timestamp", "operation", "operationParameters").show(truncate=False)
    
    def demonstrate_gdpr_compliance(self):
        """Demonstrate GDPR-compliant data deletion."""
        print("\n=== GDPR COMPLIANCE - RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN ===")
        
        gdpr_table_path = f"{self.base_path}/gdpr_demo"
        
        # Create user data table
        data = [
            (1, "Alice", "alice@email.com", "123 Main St", "555-0001", "2024-01-01"),
            (2, "Bob", "bob@email.com", "456 Oak Ave", "555-0002", "2024-01-02"),
            (3, "Charlie", "charlie@email.com", "789 Pine Rd", "555-0003", "2024-01-03")
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, [
            "user_id", "name", "email", "address", "phone", "created_at"
        ])
        
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(gdpr_table_path)
        
        print("User Data Table:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(gdpr_table_path).show()
        
        # GDPR deletion request for user_id = 2
        print("\nProcessing GDPR deletion request for user_id = 2...")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, gdpr_table_path)
        
        # Hard delete - completely remove user data
        delta_table.delete("user_id = 2")
        
        print("\nTable After GDPR Deletion:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(gdpr_table_path).show()
        
        # Verify deletion in history
        print("\nVerifying deletion in history (Time Travel):")
        print("Note: Data is deleted from current version but exists in history")
        
        history = delta_table.history()
        print(f"Total versions: {history.count()}")
        
        # To completely remove from history, need to vacuum with 0 retention
        print("\nTo completely remove from all versions (GDPR compliance):")
        print("1. Delete the data")
        print("2. Run VACUUM with 0 retention")
        print("3. This permanently removes old files")
        
        delta_table.vacuum(0)  # Remove old files immediately
        print("Vacuum completed - data permanently removed")
    
    def run_complete_delete_demo(self):
        """Run complete delete demonstration."""
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("COMPLETE DELETE PATTERN DEMONSTRATION")
        print("="*60)
        
        # Simple delete
        self.create_sample_table()
        self.perform_simple_delete()
        
        # Conditional delete
        self.create_sample_table()
        self.perform_conditional_delete()
        
        # Delete with subquery
        self.create_sample_table()
        self.perform_delete_with_subquery()
        
        # Soft delete
        self.implement_soft_delete()
        
        # Partition delete
        self.perform_partition_delete()
        
        # Delete metrics
        self.demonstrate_delete_metrics()
        
        # GDPR compliance
        self.demonstrate_gdpr_compliance()

## 7. Update Pattern

```python
"""
UPDATE PATTERN
Purpose: Modify existing rows in Delta tables with ACID guarantees.
Use Cases:
- Data corrections
- Status updates
- Incremental updates
- Computed column updates
"""

class DeltaUpdatePattern:
    def __init__(self, spark, base_path):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_path = base_path
        self.table_path = f"{base_path}/update_demo"
    
    def create_sample_table(self):
        """Create a sample table for update operations."""
        print("Creating sample table...")
        
        data = [
            (1, "Product A", 100.0, 50, "available", "2024-01-01", None),
            (2, "Product B", 150.0, 0, "available", "2024-01-02", None),
            (3, "Product C", 200.0, 30, "available", "2024-01-03", None),
            (4, "Product D", 175.0, 5, "available", "2024-01-04", None),
            (5, "Product E", 125.0, 100, "available", "2024-01-05", None),
            (6, "Product F", 90.0, 0, "available", "2024-01-06", None),
            (7, "Product G", 110.0, 75, "available", "2024-01-07", None),
            (8, "Product H", 160.0, 20, "available", "2024-01-08", None)
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, [
            "product_id", "product_name", "price", "stock_quantity", 
            "status", "created_at", "last_updated"
        ])
        
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(self.table_path)
        
        print("Sample table created")
        print("\nInitial Table:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path).show()
    
    def perform_simple_update(self):
        """Perform simple update operation."""
        print("\n=== PERFORMING SIMPLE UPDATE ===")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, self.table_path)
        
        # Update price for a specific product
        print("Updating price for Product A...")
        delta_table.update(
            condition="product_id = 1",
            set={
                "price": "110.0",
                "last_updated": "current_timestamp()"
            }
        )
        
        print("\nTable After Simple Update:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path) \
            .select("product_id", "product_name", "price", "last_updated") \
            .show()
    
    def perform_conditional_update(self):
        """Perform update with complex conditions."""
        print("\n=== PERFORMING CONDITIONAL UPDATE ===")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, self.table_path)
        
        # Update status to 'out_of_stock' where quantity is 0
        print("Updating status for out-of-stock products...")
        delta_table.update(
            condition="stock_quantity = 0",
            set={
                "status": "'out_of_stock'",
                "last_updated": "current_timestamp()"
            }
        )
        
        print("\nTable After Conditional Update:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path) \
            .select("product_id", "product_name", "stock_quantity", "status") \
            .show()
    
    def perform_computed_column_update(self):
        """Perform update with computed values."""
        print("\n=== PERFORMING COMPUTED COLUMN UPDATE ===")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, self.table_path)
        
        # Apply 10% discount to products with low stock
        print("Applying 10% discount to low-stock products...")
        delta_table.update(
            condition="stock_quantity > 0 AND stock_quantity < 25",
            set={
                "price": "price * 0.9",
                "status": "'on_sale'",
                "last_updated": "current_timestamp()"
            }
        )
        
        print("\nTable After Computed Update:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path) \
            .select("product_id", "product_name", "price", "stock_quantity", "status") \
            .orderBy("product_id") \
            .show()
    
    def perform_bulk_update(self):
        """Perform bulk update across multiple rows."""
        print("\n=== PERFORMING BULK UPDATE ===")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, self.table_path)
        
        # Increase all prices by 5%
        print("Increasing all prices by 5%...")
        delta_table.update(
            condition="status != 'out_of_stock'",
            set={
                "price": "price * 1.05",
                "last_updated": "current_timestamp()"
            }
        )
        
        print("\nTable After Bulk Update:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path) \
            .select("product_id", "product_name", "price", "status") \
            .orderBy("product_id") \
            .show()
    
    def perform_update_with_case_when(self):
        """Perform update with CASE WHEN logic."""
        print("\n=== PERFORMING UPDATE WITH CASE WHEN ===")
        
        # Reset table
        self.create_sample_table()
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, self.table_path)
        
        # Update status based on stock levels
        print("Updating status based on stock levels...")
        self.spark.sql(f"""
            UPDATE delta.`{self.table_path}`
            SET status = CASE 
                WHEN stock_quantity = 0 THEN 'out_of_stock'
                WHEN stock_quantity < 25 THEN 'low_stock'
                WHEN stock_quantity < 50 THEN 'medium_stock'
                ELSE 'in_stock'
            END,
            last_updated = current_timestamp()
        """)
        
        print("\nTable After CASE WHEN Update:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path) \
            .select("product_id", "product_name", "stock_quantity", "status") \
            .orderBy("product_id") \
            .show()
    
    def perform_update_from_another_table(self):
        """Perform update using data from another table."""
        print("\n=== PERFORMING UPDATE FROM ANOTHER TABLE ===")
        
        # Create a price update table
        price_updates = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            (1, 115.0),
            (3, 210.0),
            (5, 130.0)
        ], ["product_id", "new_price"])
        
        price_updates_path = f"{self.base_path}/price_updates"
        price_updates.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(price_updates_path)
        
        print("Price Updates Table:")
        price_updates.show()
        
        # Perform update using merge
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, self.table_path)
        updates_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, price_updates_path)
        
        delta_table.alias("target").merge(
            updates_table.toDF().alias("source"),
            "target.product_id = source.product_id"
        ).whenMatchedUpdate(set={
            "price": "source.new_price",
            "last_updated": "current_timestamp()"
        }).execute()
        
        print("\nTable After Update from Another Table:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path) \
            .select("product_id", "product_name", "price", "last_updated") \
            .orderBy("product_id") \
            .show()
    
    def

                    WHEN stock_quantity < 25 THEN price * 0.9
                    ELSE price

        print("\nTable After Conditional Column Update:")

    def demonstrate_update_with_struct(self):
        """Demonstrate updating nested/struct columns."""
        print("\n=== UPDATE WITH STRUCT COLUMNS ===")
        
        struct_table_path = f"{self.base_path}/struct_update_demo"
        
        # Create table with struct column
        from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType
        
        data = [
            (1, "Product A", {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "NYC", "zip": "10001"}, {"regular": 100.0, "sale": None}),
            (2, "Product B", {"street": "456 Oak Ave", "city": "LA", "zip": "90001"}, {"regular": 150.0, "sale": None}),
            (3, "Product C", {"street": "789 Pine Rd", "city": "Chicago", "zip": "60601"}, {"regular": 200.0, "sale": None})
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("name", StringType(), True),
            StructField("address", StructType([
                StructField("street", StringType(), True),
                StructField("city", StringType(), True),
                StructField("zip", StringType(), True)
            ]), True),
            StructField("pricing", StructType([
                StructField("regular", DoubleType(), True),
                StructField("sale", DoubleType(), True)
            ]), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(struct_table_path)
        
        print("Initial Table with Struct Columns:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(struct_table_path).show(truncate=False)
        
        # Update nested field
        print("\nUpdating nested struct fields...")
        self.spark.sql(f"""
            UPDATE delta.`{struct_table_path}`
            SET pricing.sale = pricing.regular * 0.8
            WHERE id IN (1, 2)
        """)
        
        print("\nTable After Struct Update:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(struct_table_path).show(truncate=False)

## 8. Schema Enforcement Pattern

```python
"""
SCHEMA ENFORCEMENT PATTERN
Purpose: Ensure data quality by rejecting writes that don't match the table schema.
Use Cases:
- Data quality enforcement
- Preventing schema drift
- Type safety
- Column validation
"""

class DeltaSchemaEnforcementPattern:
    def __init__(self, spark, base_path):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_path = base_path
        self.table_path = f"{base_path}/schema_enforcement_demo"
    
    def create_table_with_schema(self):
        """Create a Delta table with a defined schema."""
        print("Creating table with defined schema...")
        
        from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType, DateType
        
        # Define strict schema
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("employee_id", IntegerType(), nullable=False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), nullable=False),
            StructField("email", StringType(), nullable=False),
            StructField("department", StringType(), nullable=True),
            StructField("salary", DoubleType(), nullable=False),
            StructField("hire_date", DateType(), nullable=False)
        ])
        
        data = [
            (1, "Alice", "alice@company.com", "Engineering", 75000.0, "2024-01-01"),
            (2, "Bob", "bob@company.com", "Sales", 65000.0, "2024-01-15"),
            (3, "Charlie", "charlie@company.com", "Marketing", 70000.0, "2024-02-01")
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(self.table_path)
        
        print("Table created with schema:")
        df.printSchema()
        df.show()
    
    def demonstrate_schema_enforcement_success(self):
        """Demonstrate successful write with matching schema."""
        print("\n=== SCHEMA ENFORCEMENT - SUCCESSFUL WRITE ===")
        
        # Write data with matching schema
        new_data = [
            (4, "David", "david@company.com", "Engineering", 80000.0, "2024-03-01"),
            (5, "Eve", "eve@company.com", "HR", 72000.0, "2024-03-15")
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(new_data, [
            "employee_id", "name", "email", "department", "salary", "hire_date"
        ])
        
        print("Writing data with matching schema...")
        df.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(self.table_path)
        
        print("\nTable after successful append:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path).show()
    
    def demonstrate_schema_mismatch_column_type(self):

    def demonstrate_check_constraints(self):
        """Demonstrate CHECK constraints for advanced validation."""
        print("\n=== SCHEMA ENFORCEMENT - CHECK CONSTRAINTS ===")
        
        constraint_table_path = f"{self.base_path}/constraint_demo"
        
        # Create table
```python
        data = [
            (1, "Alice", "alice@company.com", "Engineering", 75000.0, "2024-01-01"),
            (2, "Bob", "bob@company.com", "Sales", 65000.0, "2024-01-15")

    def demonstrate_schema_validation_modes(self):
        """Demonstrate different schema validation modes."""
        print("\n=== SCHEMA VALIDATION MODES ===")
        
        mode_table_path = f"{self.base_path}/validation_mode_demo"
        
        # Create initial table
        data = [
            (1, "Product A", 100.0)
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "name", "price"])
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(mode_table_path)
        
        print("Initial table created")
        
        # Mode 1: Default (strict enforcement)
        print("\n--- Mode 1: Default Strict Enforcement ---")
        new_data = [
            (2, "Product B", 150.0, "Extra")  # Extra column
        ]
        
        df_extra = self.spark.createDataFrame(new_data, ["id", "name", "price", "category"])
        
        try:
            df_extra.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(mode_table_path)
            print("Write succeeded (unexpected)")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Write failed with strict enforcement: {type(e).__name__}")
        
        # Mode 2: mergeSchema option (allow schema evolution)
        print("\n--- Mode 2: With mergeSchema Option ---")
        print("Note: This allows schema evolution (covered in Schema Evolution pattern)")
        
        try:
            df_extra.write.format("delta") \
                .option("mergeSchema", "true") \
                .mode("append") \
                .save(mode_table_path)
            print("Write succeeded with mergeSchema option")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Write failed: {type(e).__name__}")
        
        print("\nFinal schema:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(mode_table_path).printSchema()

            StructField("score", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("is_active", BooleanType(), False)

        data = [
            (1, "Test A", 95.5, True),
            (2, "Test B", 87.3, False)
        ]

        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(type_table_path)
        
        print("Table created with strict types:")
        df.printSchema()
        
        # Test type coercion
        print("\n--- Testing Type Coercion ---")
        
        # Integer instead of Double for score
        data_int_score = [
            (3, "Test C", 90, True)  # 90 instead of 90.0
        ]
        
        df_int = self.spark.createDataFrame(data_int_score, ["id", "name", "score", "is_active"])
        
        print("Writing integer where double expected...")
        try:
            df_int.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(type_table_path)
            print("Write succeeded - Spark coerced int to double")
            
            result = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(type_table_path)
            result.show()
            result.printSchema()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Write failed: {type(e).__name__}")

## 9. Schema Evolution Pattern

```python
"""
SCHEMA EVOLUTION PATTERN
Purpose: Allow controlled schema changes while maintaining backward compatibility.
Use Cases:
- Adding new columns
- Renaming columns
- Changing data types
- Handling evolving data sources
"""

class DeltaSchemaEvolutionPattern:
    def __init__(self, spark, base_path):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_path = base_path
        self.table_path = f"{base_path}/schema_evolution_demo"
    
    def create_initial_table(self):
        """Create initial table with basic schema."""
        print("Creating initial table with basic schema...")
        
        data = [
            (1, "Product A", 100.0),
            (2, "Product B", 150.0),
            (3, "Product C", 200.0)
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, ["product_id", "product_name", "price"])
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(self.table_path)
        
        print("Initial table created:")
        df.printSchema()
        df.show()
    
    def demonstrate_add_column(self):
        """Demonstrate adding new columns to existing table."""
        print("\n=== ADDING NEW COLUMNS ===")
        
        # New data with additional column
        new_data = [
            (4, "Product D", 175.0, "Electronics"),
            (5, "Product E", 125.0, "Clothing")
        ]
        
        df_new = self.spark.createDataFrame(new_data, 
            ["product_id", "product_name", "price", "category"])
        
        print("New data with additional 'category' column:")
        df_new.printSchema()
        
        # Write with mergeSchema option
        print("\nWriting with mergeSchema option...")
        df_new.write.format("delta") \
            .option("mergeSchema", "true") \
            .mode("append") \
            .save(self.table_path)
        
        print("\nTable after adding column:")
        result = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path)
        result.printSchema()
        result.show()
        
        print("\nNote: Old records have NULL for the new column")
    
    def demonstrate_add_multiple_columns(self):
        """Demonstrate adding multiple columns at once."""
        print("\n=== ADDING MULTIPLE COLUMNS ===")
        
        # New data with multiple additional columns
        new_data = [
            (6, "Product F", 90.0, "Books", 50, True)
        ]
        
        df_new = self.spark.createDataFrame(new_data, 
            ["product_id", "product_name", "price", "category", "stock_quantity", "is_available"])
        
        print("New data with multiple additional columns:")
        df_new.printSchema()
        
        # Write with mergeSchema
        df_new.write.format("delta") \
            .option("mergeSchema", "true") \
            .mode("append") \
            .save(self.table_path)
        
        print("\nTable after adding multiple columns:")
        result = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path)
        result.printSchema()
        result.show()
    
    def demonstrate_column_reordering(self):
        """Demonstrate that column order doesn't matter with schema evolution."""
        print("\n=== COLUMN REORDERING ===")
        
        # New data with different column order
        new_data = [
            (7, "Toys", "Product G", 110.0, True, 30)
        ]
        
        df_new = self.spark.createDataFrame(new_data, 
            ["product_id", "category", "product_name", "price", "is_available", "stock_quantity"])
        
        print("New data with reordered columns:")
        df_new.printSchema()
        
        # Write with mergeSchema
        df_new.write.format("delta") \
            .option("mergeSchema", "true") \
            .mode("append") \
            .save(self.table_path)
        
        print("\nTable after write with reordered columns:")
        result = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path)
        result.show()
        
        print("\nNote: Delta Lake matches columns by name, not position")
    
    def demonstrate_alter_table_add_column(self):
        """Demonstrate adding columns using ALTER TABLE."""
        print("\n=== ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN ===")
        
        # Add column using SQL
        print("Adding 'discount_percent' column using ALTER TABLE...")
        self.spark.sql(f"""
            ALTER TABLE delta.`{self.table_path}`
            ADD COLUMNS (discount_percent DOUBLE)
        """)
        
        # Add column with comment and default
        print("Adding 'supplier_id' column with comment...")
        self.spark.sql(f"""
            ALTER TABLE delta.`{self.table_path}`
            ADD COLUMNS (supplier_id INT COMMENT 'Supplier identifier')
        """)
        
        print("\nTable after ALTER TABLE:")
        result = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.table_path)
        result.printSchema()
        result.show(5)
    
    def demonstrate_type_widening(self):
        """Demonstrate safe type widening (int to long, float to double)."""
        print("\n=== TYPE WIDENING ===")
        
        type_table_path = f"{self.base_path}/type_widening_demo"
        
        # Create table with INT column
        data = [
            (1, "Item A", 100),
            (2, "Item B", 200)
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "name", "quantity"])
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(type_table_path)
        
        print("Initial table with INT quantity:")
        df.printSchema()
        
        # Try to write LONG values
        new_data = [
            (3, "Item C", 3000000000)  # Value too large for INT
        ]
        
        df_long = self.spark.createDataFrame(new_data, ["id", "name", "quantity"])
        
        print("\nWriting LONG values with mergeSchema...")
        df_long.write.format("delta") \
            .option("mergeSchema", "true") \
            .mode("append") \
            .save(type_table_path)
        
        print("\nTable after type widening:")
        result = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(type_table_path)
        result.printSchema()
        result.show()
    
    def demonstrate_nested_schema_evolution(self):
        """Demonstrate schema evolution with nested structures."""
        print("\n=== NESTED SCHEMA EVOLUTION ===")
        
        nested_table_path = f"{self.base_path}/nested_evolution_demo"
        
        # Create
```python
 table with nested structure
        from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType
        
        data = [
            (1, "Product A", {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "NYC"}),
            (2, "Product B", {"street": "456 Oak Ave", "city": "LA"})
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("name", StringType(), True),
            StructField("address", StructType([
                StructField("street", StringType(), True),
                StructField("city", StringType(), True)
            ]), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(nested_table_path)
        
        print("Initial nested table:")
        df.printSchema()
        df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Add field to nested structure
        new_data = [
            (3, "Product C", {"street": "789 Pine Rd", "city": "Chicago", "zip": "60601", "country": "USA"})
        ]
        
        new_schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("name", StringType(), True),
            StructField("address", StructType([
                StructField("street", StringType(), True),
                StructField("city", StringType(), True),
                StructField("zip", StringType(), True),
                StructField("country", StringType(), True)
            ]), True)
        ])
        
        df_new = self.spark.createDataFrame(new_data, new_schema)
        
        print("\nNew data with additional nested fields:")
        df_new.printSchema()
        
        # Write with mergeSchema
        df_new.write.format("delta") \
            .option("mergeSchema", "true") \
            .mode("append") \
            .save(nested_table_path)
        
        print("\nTable after nested schema evolution:")
        result = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(nested_table_path)
        result.printSchema()
        result.show(truncate=False)
    
    def demonstrate_overwrite_schema(self):
        """Demonstrate completely replacing schema with overwriteSchema."""
        print("\n=== OVERWRITE SCHEMA ===")
        
        overwrite_table_path = f"{self.base_path}/overwrite_schema_demo"
        
        # Create initial table
        data = [
            (1, "Old A", 100),
            (2, "Old B", 200)
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "old_name", "old_value"])
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(overwrite_table_path)
        
        print("Initial table:")
        df.printSchema()
        df.show()
        
        # Completely new schema
        new_data = [
            (1, "New A", 150.5, "Category A"),
            (2, "New B", 250.5, "Category B")
        ]
        
        df_new = self.spark.createDataFrame(new_data, ["id", "new_name", "new_value", "category"])
        
        print("\nNew data with completely different schema:")
        df_new.printSchema()
        
        # Overwrite with new schema
        print("\nOverwriting with new schema...")
        df_new.write.format("delta") \
            .option("overwriteSchema", "true") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .save(overwrite_table_path)
        
        print("\nTable after schema overwrite:")
        result = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(overwrite_table_path)
        result.printSchema()
        result.show()
        
        print("\nNote: Old data is completely replaced")
    
    def demonstrate_schema_evolution_with_partitions(self):
        """Demonstrate schema evolution with partitioned tables."""
        print("\n=== SCHEMA EVOLUTION WITH PARTITIONS ===")
        
        partition_table_path = f"{self.base_path}/partition_evolution_demo"
        
        # Create partitioned table
        data = [
            (1, "Product A", 100.0, "2024-01"),
            (2, "Product B", 150.0, "2024-01"),
            (3, "Product C", 200.0, "2024-02")
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "name", "price", "month"])
        df.write.format("delta") \
            .partitionBy("month") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .save(partition_table_path)
        
        print("Initial partitioned table:")
        df.printSchema()
        df.show()
        
        # Add column to partitioned table
        new_data = [
            (4, "Product D", 175.0, "2024-03", "Electronics"),
            (5, "Product E", 125.0, "2024-03", "Clothing")
        ]
        
        df_new = self.spark.createDataFrame(new_data, ["id", "name", "price", "month", "category"])
        
        print("\nAdding new column to partitioned table...")
        df_new.write.format("delta") \
            .partitionBy("month") \
            .option("mergeSchema", "true") \
            .mode("append") \
            .save(partition_table_path)
        
        print("\nTable after schema evolution:")
        result = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(partition_table_path)
        result.printSchema()
        result.orderBy("id").show()
        
        print("\nPartition structure maintained with new schema")
    
    def demonstrate_schema_evolution_best_practices(self):
        """Demonstrate best practices for schema evolution."""
        print("\n=== SCHEMA EVOLUTION BEST PRACTICES ===")
        
        best_practice_path = f"{self.base_path}/best_practice_demo"
        
        # 1. Always use explicit schemas
        print("\n1. Use Explicit Schemas")
        from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType
        
        schema_v1 = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), False)
        ])
        
        data = [(1, "Item A", 100.0), (2, "Item B", 200.0)]
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema_v1)
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(best_practice_path)
        
        print("Created table with explicit schema")
        df.printSchema()
        
        # 2. Add columns with default values
        print("\n2. Add Columns with Default Values")
        
        # Use COALESCE or default in application logic
        new_data = [(3, "Item C", 300.0)]
        df_new = self.spark.createDataFrame(new_data, ["id", "name", "value"])
        
        # Add new column with default value
        df_with_default = df_new.withColumn("status", lit("active")) \
                                 .withColumn("created_at", current_timestamp())
        
        df_with_default.write.format("delta") \
            .option("mergeSchema", "true") \
            .mode("append") \
            .save(best_practice_path)
        
        print("Added columns with default values:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(best_practice_path).show()
        
        # 3. Document schema changes
        print("\n3. Document Schema Changes in Table Properties")
        
        self.spark.sql(f"""
            ALTER TABLE delta.`{best_practice_path}`
            SET TBLPROPERTIES (
                'schema_version' = '2',
                'last_schema_change' = '2024-01-15',
                'schema_change_description' = 'Added status and created_at columns'
            )
        """)
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, best_practice_path)
        properties = delta_table.detail().select("properties").collect()[0][0]
        
        print("\nTable properties:")
        for key, value in properties.items():
            if 'schema' in key.lower():
                print(f"  {key}: {value}")
        
        # 4. Validate schema before writing
        print("\n4. Validate Schema Before Writing")
        
        def validate_schema_compatibility(new_df, table_path):
            """Validate that new schema is compatible with existing table."""
            try:
                existing_df = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(table_path)
                existing_cols = set(existing_df.columns)
                new_cols = set(new_df.columns)
                
                # Check for removed columns
                removed_cols = existing_cols - new_cols
                if removed_cols:
                    print(f"  Warning: Columns will be removed: {removed_cols}")
                    return False
                
                # Check for added columns
                added_cols = new_cols - existing_cols
                if added_cols:
                    print(f"  Info: New columns will be added: {added_cols}")
                
                return True
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  Error validating schema: {e}")
                return False
        
        test_data = [(4, "Item D", 400.0, "active", "2024-01-20")]
        df_test = self.spark.createDataFrame(test_data, 
            ["id", "name", "value", "status", "created_at"])
        
        print("\nValidating schema compatibility:")
        is_compatible = validate_schema_compatibility(df_test, best_practice_path)
        print(f"  Schema compatible: {is_compatible}")
    
    def demonstrate_schema_evolution_rollback(self):
        """Demonstrate rolling back schema changes using time travel."""
        print("\n=== SCHEMA EVOLUTION ROLLBACK ===")
        
        rollback_path = f"{self.base_path}/rollback_demo"
        
        # Version 1: Initial schema
        data_v1 = [(1, "Item A", 100.0)]
        df_v1 = self.spark.createDataFrame(data_v1, ["id", "name", "price"])
        df_v1.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(rollback_path)
        
        print("Version 1 - Initial schema:")
        df_v1.printSchema()
        
        # Version 2: Add column
        data_v2 = [(2, "Item B", 200.0, "Category A")]
        df_v2 = self.spark.createDataFrame(data_v2, ["id", "name", "price", "category"])
        df_v2.write.format("delta") \
            .option("mergeSchema", "true") \
            .mode("append") \
            .save(rollback_path)
        
        print("\nVersion 2 - Added category column:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(rollback_path).printSchema()
        
        # Version 3: Add another column
        data_v3 = [(3, "Item C", 300.0, "Category B", "Supplier X")]
        df_v3 = self.spark.createDataFrame(data_v3, ["id", "name", "price", "category", "supplier"])
        df_v3.write.format("delta") \
            .option("mergeSchema", "true") \
            .mode("append") \
            .save(rollback_path)
        
        print("\nVersion 3 - Added supplier column:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(rollback_path).printSchema()
        
        # Show history
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, rollback_path)
        print("\nTable History:")
        delta_table.history().select("version", "timestamp", "operation").show()
        
        # Rollback to version 1
        print("\nRolling back to Version 1...")
        self.spark.sql(f"RESTORE delta.`{rollback_path}` TO VERSION AS OF 1")
        
        print("\nSchema after rollback:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(rollback_path).printSchema()
        
        print("\nData after rollback:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(rollback_path).show()
    
    def run_complete_schema_evolution_demo(self):
        """Run complete schema evolution demonstration."""
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("COMPLETE SCHEMA EVOLUTION PATTERN DEMONSTRATION")
        print("="*60)
        
        # Create initial table
        self.create_initial_table()
        
        # Add single column
        self.demonstrate_add_column()
        
        # Add multiple columns
        self.demonstrate_add_multiple_columns()
        
        # Column reordering
        self.demonstrate_column_reordering()
        
        # ALTER TABLE
        self.demonstrate_alter_table_add_column()
        
        # Type widening
        self.demonstrate_type_widening()
        
        # Nested schema evolution
        self.demonstrate_nested_schema_evolution()
        
        # Overwrite schema
        self.demonstrate_overwrite_schema()
        
        # Partitioned table evolution
        self.demonstrate_schema_evolution_with_partitions()
        
        # Best practices
        self.demonstrate_schema_evolution_best_practices()
        
        # Rollback
        self.demonstrate_schema_evolution_rollback()

# Execute Schema Evolution Pattern
schema_evolution = DeltaSchemaEvolutionPattern(spark, "/tmp/delta_patterns")
schema_evolution.run_complete_schema_evolution_demo()

## 10. ACID Transaction Pattern

```python
"""
ACID TRANSACTION PATTERN
Purpose: Demonstrate ACID (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) guarantees.
Use Cases:
- Financial transactions
- Critical data operations
- Multi-step operations
- Data consistency requirements
"""

class DeltaACIDTransactionPattern:
    def __init__(self, spark, base_path):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_path = base_path
        self.table_path = f"{base_path}/acid_demo"
    
    def demonstrate_atomicity(self):
        """Demonstrate atomicity - all or nothing."""
        print("\n=== ATOMICITY DEMONSTRATION ===")
        
        atomicity_path = f"{self.base_path}/atomicity_demo"
        
        # Create initial table
        data = [
            (1, "Account A", 1000.0),
            (2, "Account B", 500.0)
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, ["account_id", "account_name", "balance"])
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(atomicity_path)
        
        print("Initial balances:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(atomicity_path).show()
        
        # Simulate a transaction that should fail
        print("\nAttempting transaction with invalid data...")
        
        try:
            # This batch includes invalid data
            invalid_data = [
                (3, "Account C", 200.0),
                (4, "Account D", "invalid_balance"),  # This will cause failure
                (5, "Account E", 300.0)
            ]
            
            df_invalid = self.spark.createDataFrame
```python
(invalid_data, ["account_id", "account_name", "balance"])
            df_invalid.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(atomicity_path)
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Transaction failed as expected: {type(e).__name__}")
            print("No partial data was written (Atomicity guaranteed)")
        
        print("\nBalances after failed transaction (unchanged):")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(atomicity_path).show()
        
        # Successful atomic transaction
        print("\nPerforming successful atomic transaction...")
        valid_data = [
            (3, "Account C", 200.0),
            (4, "Account D", 150.0),
            (5, "Account E", 300.0)
        ]
        
        df_valid = self.spark.createDataFrame(valid_data, ["account_id", "account_name", "balance"])
        df_valid.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(atomicity_path)
        
        print("\nBalances after successful transaction:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(atomicity_path).show()
        
        print("\nAll 3 records added atomically (all or nothing)")
    
    def demonstrate_consistency(self):
        """Demonstrate consistency - constraints are maintained."""
        print("\n=== CONSISTENCY DEMONSTRATION ===")
        
        consistency_path = f"{self.base_path}/consistency_demo"
        
        # Create table with constraints
        data = [
            (1, "Product A", 100.0, 50),
            (2, "Product B", 150.0, 30)
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "name", "price", "quantity"])
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(consistency_path)
        
        # Add CHECK constraint
        self.spark.sql(f"""
            ALTER TABLE delta.`{consistency_path}`
            ADD CONSTRAINT positive_price CHECK (price > 0)
        """)
        
        self.spark.sql(f"""
            ALTER TABLE delta.`{consistency_path}`
            ADD CONSTRAINT positive_quantity CHECK (quantity >= 0)
        """)
        
        print("Table created with constraints:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(consistency_path).show()
        
        # Try to violate consistency
        print("\nAttempting to violate price constraint...")
        invalid_data = [(3, "Product C", -50.0, 20)]
        df_invalid = self.spark.createDataFrame(invalid_data, ["id", "name", "price", "quantity"])
        
        try:
            df_invalid.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(consistency_path)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Write failed - Consistency maintained: {type(e).__name__}")
        
        print("\nTable remains consistent (constraint violation prevented):")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(consistency_path).show()
        
        # Demonstrate consistency with MERGE
        print("\nDemonstrating consistency with MERGE operation...")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, consistency_path)
        
        # Update that maintains consistency
        updates = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            (1, "Product A", 120.0, 45)
        ], ["id", "name", "price", "quantity"])
        
        delta_table.alias("target").merge(
            updates.alias("source"),
            "target.id = source.id"
        ).whenMatchedUpdate(set={
            "price": "source.price",
            "quantity": "source.quantity"
        }).execute()
        
        print("\nTable after consistent MERGE:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(consistency_path).show()
    
    def demonstrate_isolation(self):
        """Demonstrate isolation - concurrent operations don't interfere."""
        print("\n=== ISOLATION DEMONSTRATION ===")
        
        isolation_path = f"{self.base_path}/isolation_demo"
        
        # Create initial table
        data = [
            (1, "Record A", 100, "2024-01-01"),
            (2, "Record B", 200, "2024-01-01"),
            (3, "Record C", 300, "2024-01-01")
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "name", "value", "date"])
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(isolation_path)
        
        print("Initial table:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(isolation_path).show()
        
        # Show isolation through version history
        print("\nPerforming multiple isolated transactions...")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, isolation_path)
        
        # Transaction 1: Update
        delta_table.update(
            condition="id = 1",
            set={"value": "150"}
        )
        
        # Transaction 2: Insert
        new_data = [(4, "Record D", 400, "2024-01-02")]
        df_new = self.spark.createDataFrame(new_data, ["id", "name", "value", "date"])
        df_new.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(isolation_path)
        
        # Transaction 3: Delete
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, isolation_path)
        delta_table.delete("id = 2")
        
        print("\nFinal table after isolated transactions:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(isolation_path).show()
        
        # Show transaction history
        print("\nTransaction history (each operation is isolated):")
        delta_table.history().select("version", "timestamp", "operation", "isolationLevel").show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\nEach transaction sees a consistent snapshot of the data")
    
    def demonstrate_durability(self):
        """Demonstrate durability - committed changes persist."""
        print("\n=== DURABILITY DEMONSTRATION ===")
        
        durability_path = f"{self.base_path}/durability_demo"
        
        # Create and commit data
        data = [
            (1, "Transaction 1", "committed"),
            (2, "Transaction 2", "committed")
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "description", "status"])
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(durability_path)
        
        print("Data written and committed:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(durability_path).show()
        
        # Simulate "crash" by creating new Spark session
        print("\nSimulating system restart (new Spark session)...")
        
        # Read with new Delta table instance
        delta_table_new = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, durability_path)
        
        print("\nData persists after restart (Durability):")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(durability_path).show()
        
        # Show transaction log
        print("\nTransaction log ensures durability:")
        delta_table_new.history().select("version", "timestamp", "operation").show()
        
        # Add more data
        new_data = [(3, "Transaction 3", "committed")]
        df_new = self.spark.createDataFrame(new_data, ["id", "description", "status"])
        df_new.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(durability_path)
        
        print("\nAll committed transactions are durable:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(durability_path).show()
    
    def demonstrate_multi_step_transaction(self):
        """Demonstrate multi-step transaction with rollback capability."""
        print("\n=== MULTI-STEP TRANSACTION ===")
        
        transaction_path = f"{self.base_path}/multi_step_demo"
        
        # Create accounts table
        accounts_data = [
            (1, "Alice", 1000.0),
            (2, "Bob", 500.0),
            (3, "Charlie", 750.0)
        ]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(accounts_data, ["account_id", "name", "balance"])
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(transaction_path)
        
        print("Initial account balances:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(transaction_path).show()
        
        # Record version before transaction
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, transaction_path)
        version_before = delta_table.history(1).select("version").collect()[0][0]
        print(f"\nVersion before transaction: {version_before}")
        
        # Multi-step transaction: Transfer money from Alice to Bob
        print("\nExecuting multi-step transaction: Transfer $200 from Alice to Bob")
        
        try:
            # Step 1: Debit Alice's account
            delta_table.update(
                condition="account_id = 1",
                set={"balance": "balance - 200"}
            )
            
            # Step 2: Credit Bob's account
            delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, transaction_path)
            delta_table.update(
                condition="account_id = 2",
                set={"balance": "balance + 200"}
            )
            
            print("\nTransaction completed successfully:")
            self.spark.read.format("delta").load(transaction_path).show()
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Transaction failed: {e}")
            print("Rolling back to previous version...")
            self.spark.sql(f"RESTORE delta.`{transaction_path}` TO VERSION AS OF {version_before}")
        
        # Show transaction history
        print("\nTransaction history:")
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, transaction_path)
        delta_table.history().select("version", "timestamp", "operation", "operationMetrics").show(truncate=False)
    
    def demonstrate_optimistic_concurrency_control(self):
        """Demonstrate optimistic concurrency control."""
        print("\n=== OPTIMISTIC CONCURRENCY CONTROL ===")
        
        concurrency_path = f"{self.base_path}/concurrency_demo"
        
        # Create initial table
        data = [(1, "Resource A", 100, 0)]
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "name", "value", "version"])
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(concurrency_path)
        
        print("Initial state:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(concurrency_path).show()
        
        # Simulate two concurrent updates
        print("\nSimulating concurrent updates with version checking...")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, concurrency_path)
        
        # Reader 1 reads current state
        current_state = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(concurrency_path).collect()[0]
        current_version = current_state["version"]
        current_value = current_state["value"]
        
        print(f"Reader 1 sees: value={current_value}, version={current_version}")
        
        # Writer 1 updates (succeeds)
        delta_table.update(
            condition=f"id = 1 AND version = {current_version}",
            set={
                "value": str(current_value + 50),
                "version": str(current_version + 1)
            }
        )
        
        print("\nWriter 1 update succeeded:")
        self.spark.read.format("delta").load(concurrency_path).show()
        
        # Writer 2 tries to update with stale version (fails)
        print("\nWriter 2 attempts update with stale version...")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, concurrency_path)
        delta_table.update(
            condition=f"id = 1 AND version = {current_version}",  # Stale version
            set={
                "value": str(current_value + 30),
                "version": str(current_version + 1)
            }
        )
        
        print("\nWriter 2 update failed (no rows matched - version conflict):")
        result = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(concurrency_path)
        result.show()
        
        # Check metrics
        metrics = delta_table.history(1).select("operationMetrics").collect()[0][0]
        print(f"Rows updated by Writer 2: {metrics.get('numUpdatedRows', 0)}")
    
    def demonstrate_transaction_log(self):
        """Demonstrate the transaction log structure."""
        print("\n=== TRANSACTION LOG DEMONSTRATION ===")
        
        log_path = f"{self.base_path}/transaction_log_demo"
        
        # Create table and perform various operations
        data = [(1, "Record 1", "initial")]
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "name", "status"])
        df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(log_path)
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, log_path)
        
        # Perform various operations
        operations = [
            ("INSERT", lambda: self.spark.createDataFrame([(2, "Record 2", "new")], ["id", "name", "status"])
                .write.format("delta").mode("append").save(log_path)),
            ("UPDATE", lambda: DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, log_path)
                .update(condition="id = 1", set={"status": "'updated'"})),
            ("DELETE", lambda: DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, log_path)
                .delete("id = 2")),
            ("MERGE", lambda: DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, log_path).alias("target").merge(
                self.spark.createDataFrame([(3, "Record 3", "merged")], ["id", "name", "status"]).alias("source"),
                "target.id = source.id"
            ).whenNotMatchedInsert(values={"id": "source.id", "name": "source.name", "status": "source.status"}).execute())
        ]
        
        for op_name, op_func in operations:
            op_func()
            print(f"{op_name} operation completed")
        
        # Show complete transaction log
        print("\nComplete Transaction Log:")
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, log_path)
        delta_table.history().select(
            "version", 
            "timestamp", 
            "operation", 
            "operationParameters",
            "operationMetrics"
        ).show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\nEach operation is logged with full details for ACID compliance")
    
    def run_complete_acid_demo(self):
        """Run complete ACID transaction demonstration."""
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("COMPLETE ACID TRANSACTION PATTERN DEMONSTRATION")
        print("="*60)
        
        # Atomicity
        self.demonstrate_atomicity()
        
        # Consistency
        self.demonstrate_consistency()
        
        # Isolation
        self.demonstrate_isolation()
        
        # Durability
        self.demonstrate_durability()
        
        # Multi-step transaction
        self.demonstrate_multi_step_transaction()
        
        # Optimistic concurrency control
        self.demonstrate_optimistic_concurrency_control()
        
        # Transaction log
        self.demonstrate_transaction_log()

# Execute ACID Transaction Pattern
acid_pattern = DeltaACIDTransactionPattern(spark, "/tmp/delta_patterns")
acid_pattern.run_complete_acid_demo()
